text: Neutron’s Stage 2 and Thrust Module have arrived to Launch Complex 3 – another major step forward for the team that brings us closer to Neutron’s debut.
98 launches in. The view never gets old. 📸 angus bodle

Giving future space missions a leg up. Or an arm, rather. Rocket Lab Robotics developed a robotic arm with NASA that can walk across spacecraft, use tools, and perform repairs and upgrades in orbit. It launches on NASA's Fly Foundational Robots mission in late 2027. https://t.co/G9jf2fx4KD

Before we go to space, we set sail 🚢 This week Neutron’s stage 2 and thrust module travelled from Middle River to Launch Complex 3 within the Mid-Atlantic Regional Spaceport in Wallops, Virginia. Here's a glimpse behind the scenes.
Triple digits unlocked. 💯 🚀 The 100th Electron has left the factory, headed for launch. Thank you and congratulations to the many people behind this rocket, and the 99 before it.

Less than a week ago our 98th Electron delivered mission success for hawkeye360 with another flawless launch. Up next: Our 99th launch is scheduled next week and our 100th rocket is close behind, scheduled for delivery to Launch Complex 1 soon.

Make parts that go to space 🚀 We’re hiring CNC Operators and Programmers in Auckland, New Zealand, and Long Beach, CA. Be part of the high performance team bringing designs for spacecraft and rockets to life using advanced manufacturing technology.

Neutron’s Stage 2 and Thrust Module have arrived to Virginia. After a short barge ride from the Neutron Factory, these major assemblies have now been offloaded on Wallops Island and are going through arrival checkouts. Next up: integrated fluids testing and launch mount interface checkouts for the Thrust Module, with Stage 2 to follow on the test stand beside it soon after.
